newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe to sell 70 percent stake in steelworks.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe to sell 70 percent stake in steelworks.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government will give up 70 percent of its shareholding in the ailing national steelworks, ZISCO, when it finally privatises it, Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan Shamuyarira said on Thursday.

Shamuyarira told Reuters the government would privatise the Zimbabwe Iron and Steel Company (Zisco), Africa's largest steelworks outside South Africa, after completing at the end of next year a Z$2.2 billion (U.S.$193 million) rehabilitation due to start next month.
"After privatising, the government will remain with (a) 30 percent (stake in Zisco)," he told Reuters.
He and Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa did not say how the government would raise the money needed for the rehabilitation plan.
Earlier, Shamuyarira told local industrialists at their annual congress in the northern resort town of Victoria Falls that the steel company would be privatised through tender.
Finance Minister Murerwa told the congress that ZISCO -- which has been tottering for years under management, financial and production problems -- had to be turned around before privatising.
He said an international privatisation tender invitation early this year had failed to attract investment into ZISCO because of the problems it was experiencing.
"Unless it's turned around we are not going to get an equity partner for Zisco," he said.

He said the 18-month rehabilitation programme would include reviving the steelworks' main Blast Furnace Four which has not been working properly for almost seven years and accounts for 70 percent of ZISCO's production.
Shamuyarira said work on the furnace had started with Chinese financial aid of U.S.$35 million, with the Zimbabwe government providing the remaining U.S.$15 million needed to finish the job.
